title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو يدعو إلى إصلاح حقيقي ونهضة شاملة
title_en: His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew Calls for Genuine Reform and a Comprehensive Revival
body_ar: دعا فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء - في كلمته التي ألقاها بمقاطعة واد الناقة - إلى إصلاح حقيقي في المجتمع يقوم كل فرد بمجهود فيه، كما دعا إلى نهضة حضارية وثقافية شاملة وإحداث قطيعة تامة مع المسلكيات البدوية المشينة. وقال حفظه الله: إن بلدنا يحتاج إلى كثير من الجهود لتغيير حاله، والتغيير يبدأ من الفرد أولا ...". وتساءل فضيلتة قائلا: "إلى متى ونحن أهل بادية ؟! .. إلى متى ونحن نعيش على ما تعيش عليه المجتمعات المتخلفة"؟ !. وأشار فضيلته إلى أن من المسلكيات المتخلفة عدم العناية بصحة الأطفال والصحة العامة وكذلك السلوك البدوي فى السكن الذي يؤدى إلى مشاكل كثيرة فلا بد من التخطيط العمراني العصري للمساكن، والسعي الجاد لمحاربة الأمية وإشاعة ثقافة التمدرس وحياة العلم والتعلم. وأكد فضيلة الشيخ على ضرورة ممارسة كل فرد لأي نشاط مفيد، وتجاوز النظرة الدونية للمهن ونبذ الطبقية، فكل مهنة مهما كانت يمكن أن تدفع بالمجتمع إلى الرفاهية والسعادة، وفي نفس السياق حث النساء خصوصا على العمل المنتج بإقامة التعاونيات في شتى المجالات ( الخياطة وغيرها ..). وقد حضر هذه المحاضرة حاكم واد الناقة وعمدتها وجمهور غفير من سكان المقاطعة ووجهائها. ونشير في هذا السياق إلى أن هذه المحاضرة نُظّمت مساء الأربعاء 06/04/2011، من طرف جمعية المستقبل للدعوة والثقافة والتعليم التي يرأسها فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو حفظه الله.
body_en:
His eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew, head of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars — in an address he delivered in the district of Wad Naqah — called for a genuine reform in society in which every individual makes an effort, and likewise called for a comprehensive civilisational and cultural revival, and for a complete break with disgraceful bedouin patterns of conduct. He said, may God preserve him: "Our country needs a great deal of effort to change its condition, and change begins with the individual first ...". His eminence asked: "How long are we to be people of the desert?! .. How long are we to live as backward societies live?!"

His eminence indicated that among the backward patterns of conduct are the neglect of children's health and of public health, and likewise bedouin behaviour in housing, which leads to many problems; so there must be modern urban planning for dwellings, and a serious effort to combat illiteracy and to spread the culture of schooling and of a life of learning and study. His eminence the Sheikh affirmed the necessity that every individual practise some useful activity, that the demeaning view of the trades be got past, and that class distinction be cast off; for every trade, whatever it may be, can push society towards prosperity and happiness. In the same connection he urged women in particular to productive work, by setting up cooperatives in various fields (tailoring and others ..).

This lecture was attended by the governor of Wad Naqah and its mayor, and by a large audience of the district's inhabitants and its notables. We note in this connection that this lecture was organised on the evening of Wednesday 06/04/2011 by the Future Association for Da'wah, Culture and Education, which is headed by his eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, may God preserve him.

flags.arabic: قطيعة تامة مع المسلكيات البدوية المشينة ... إلى متى ونحن أهل بادية ؟! ... السلوك البدوي فى السكن
flags.context: the record's central theme, and the third instance of it in this slice
options: translate literally and refer the phrasing upward for a decision
flags.note: Editorially sensitive, and this is the sharpest of three instances in this slice — the others are 'negative bedouinism' in record 671 and 'an unsatisfactory bedouin behaviour' in record 679. Here the summary has him call for a complete break with 'disgraceful bedouin patterns of conduct' and ask how long 'we' are to be people of the desert. Two things should be visible to whoever decides on publication. First, the first person: he is speaking to and about his own society, not describing another people. Second, everything he is said to criticise is a practice — health neglect, unplanned housing, illiteracy — not an ancestry. In flat English, and lifted out of the item, the phrase reads as contempt for an ethnic group. Translated literally, neither softened nor sharpened; the rendering of 'بدوي' should be settled consistently across all three records at once.

flags.arabic: وتجاوز النظرة الدونية للمهن ونبذ الطبقية
flags.context: the call regarding trades and social class
options: the demeaning view of the trades, and class distinction
the low regard for manual occupations, and the caste system
social snobbery about work, and social stratification
flags.note: Editorially sensitive in the Mauritanian setting, where hereditary occupational rank is a live and legally fraught subject. 'الطبقية' is the general word for stratification by class and is rendered as such; the English deliberately does NOT reach for 'caste', which would make a specific and contested claim about Mauritanian society that the Arabic does not make here. A reviewer with the recording should confirm the Sheikh's own word, since this is the editor's summary and the choice between these renderings carries real weight.

flags.context: the first quotation attributed to the Sheikh
options: preserve the ellipsis and the unmatched quotation mark as served
flags.note: The quotation closes with an ellipsis and a closing quotation mark that has no opening pair, so words appear to have been dropped from a longer quotation and the quotation's beginning is not marked. The English preserves the ellipsis. Note also 'فضيلتة' for 'فضيلته', and 'فى' and 'يؤدى' written with dotless yāʾ in Egyptian style beside the dotted form elsewhere in the same sentence; all left as served.

translator_notes: A site news summary of an address, not a text by the Sheikh; everything is second-hand except the two passages the report puts in quotation marks.
'واد الناقة' (Wad Naqah) is a district south-east of Nouakchott; the romanisation should be checked against the Sheikh's office's preferred spelling.

The page ends with a navigation line inviting the reader to click through to the recording in the site's separate media system; it is a site affordance rather than content and is not part of body_ar or body_en.
